practiceQuestions.q: Who among the following was the original founder of the Sur Empire who defeated Humayun in the battles of Chausa and Kannauj?
practiceQuestions.sol: Sher Khan, later known as Sher Shah Suri, was a brilliant strategist and administrator who challenged Mughal authority, ultimately defeating Humayun at Chausa (1539) and Kannauj (1540) to establish the Sur dynasty. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 Themes in Indian History - Part II]

practiceQuestions.q: In which year did the decisive Battle of Chausa take place between Humayun and Sher Khan?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Battle of Chausa was fought on June 26, 1539, near Buxar, where Sher Khan decisively defeated Humayun, forcing him to flee for his life. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 History]

practiceQuestions.q: The Battle of Kannauj, also known as the Battle of Bilgram, which completely ousted Humayun from India, was fought in:
practiceQuestions.sol: The Battle of Kannauj (Bilgram) took place on May 17, 1540. Following this defeat, Humayun became a prince without a kingdom and wandered in exile for 15 years. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 History]

practiceQuestions.q: Which strategic fortress did Sher Khan capture in 1538, securing immense wealth and consolidating his power base before confronting Humayun?
practiceQuestions.sol: Sher Khan cleverly seized the impregnable Rohtas Fort in Bihar in 1538 through a stratagem, providing him a safe refuge for his family and accumulated wealth. [Primary Reference: Standard Medieval History Sources, Satish Chandra]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the original name of Sher Khan before he assumed the title of Sher Shah?
practiceQuestions.sol: Sher Shah's original name was Farid Khan. He earned the title 'Sher Khan' after killing a tiger single-handedly while serving under the Afghan ruler of Bihar, Bahar Khan Lohani. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 History]

practiceQuestions.q: During Humayun's campaign in Bengal, what name did Humayun temporarily give to the city of Gaur after capturing it?
practiceQuestions.sol: After capturing Gaur, the capital of Bengal, Humayun spent months in merrymaking and renamed it Jannatabad (Heavenly City), while Sher Khan cut off his communications with Agra. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: Who saved Humayun's life by offering him a water-skin (leather bag) to float across the Ganges after the defeat at the Battle of Chausa?
practiceQuestions.sol: During his escape from Chausa, Humayun's horse sank in the Ganges. A water-carrier (bhisti) named Nizam helped him cross using an inflated water-skin, for which Humayun later rewarded him symbolically. [Primary Reference: Standard Historical Accounts/Abul Fazl's Akbarnama]

practiceQuestions.q: Which of Humayun's brothers declared himself independent at Agra during the crisis of the Bengal campaign and Sher Khan's rebellion?
practiceQuestions.sol: Hindal Mirza left his post in Bengal, went to Agra, and even had the Khutba read in his own name, severely undermining Mughal unity against Sher Khan. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 History]

practiceQuestions.q: The Treaty of Chunar (1531/1532) was signed between Humayun and which commander, though it failed to permanently resolve hostilities?
practiceQuestions.sol: Early in his reign (1531-1532), Humayun besieged Chunar Fort held by Sher Khan. An agreement was reached where Sher Khan submitted nominally, but it was merely a tactical truce before the major showdown. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: After losing the Battle of Kannauj, Humayun sought refuge outside India. Which Persian ruler provided him military assistance to help reconquer Delhi in 1555?
practiceQuestions.sol: Humayun fled to the Safavid court of Shah Tahmasp in Persia. With Shah Tahmasp's military backing, Humayun later captured Kandahar, Kabul, and eventually reconquered Delhi in 1555. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 History]

practiceQuestions.q: How did Humayun's strategic miscalculation in embarking on the prolonged Bengal campaign alter the balance of power in Northern India?
opts: It allowed Gujarat to merge with Malwa, creating an invincible confederacy.
It gave Sher Khan unhindered operational freedom to cut Mughal supply lines, seize imperial treasuries, and consolidate Afghan forces.
It forced the Portuguese to ally with the Mughals, alienating regional Sultanates.
It resulted in an immediate financial surplus that enabled Humayun to hire European mercenaries.
practiceQuestions.sol: Humayun's march to Bengal lacked long-term strategic depth. While he was bogged down in Gaur, Sher Khan systematically cut off communications with Agra, looted Bihar and Jaunpur, and mobilized Afghan nationalism against the Mughals. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the core tactical superiority that enabled Sher Khan to outmaneuver the Mughal forces during the campaign of 1537-1540?
opts: Possession of superior Portuguese naval fleets in the Gangetic delta
Mastery of mobile guerrilla warfare, strategic deception, and leveraging local Afghan support networks
Unconditional financial backing from the Ottoman Empire
Use of European-style heavy artillery that outranged Mughal cannons
practiceQuestions.sol: Sher Khan avoided pitched frontal battles when the Mughal military machine was cohesive, opting for hit-and-run tactics, exhaustion of enemy supplies, psychological warfare, and securing impregnable bases like Rohtas. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 History]

practiceQuestions.q: How did the political fragmentation and ambitions of Humayun's brothers (Kamran, Askari, and Hindal) contribute to the Mughal collapse against Sher Khan?
opts: They provided unlimited troops to Sher Khan in exchange for territorial autonomy.
Their failure to provide unified military reinforcement and their internal rivalries left Humayun diplomatically and militarily isolated.
They successfully defeated Sher Khan in Punjab, but refused to share the spoils with Humayun.
They assassinated the Mughal vizier, causing a complete administrative paralysis.
practiceQuestions.sol: Unlike Babur, who enjoyed a unified family and loyal commanders, Humayun faced severe fratricidal friction. Kamran held Punjab and refused to commit troops effectively, while Hindal rebelled in Agra, fracturing the Mughal defense apparatus. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: The rise of Sher Khan represents a resurgence of which sociopolitical force in Northern Indian politics?
opts: Rajput confederacy seeking independence from Delhi
Afghan nobility seeking to reclaim political hegemony lost to the Mughals in 1526
Deccani Sultanates expanding northward into Hindustan
Religious reformist movements challenging both Sunni orthodoxy and Mughal legitimacy
practiceQuestions.sol: Sher Khan's campaign was built on the foundation of Afghan pride and solidarity. He skillfully mobilized scattered Afghan chiefs who had been displaced following Ibrahim Lodi's defeat at Panipat in 1526. [Primary Reference: NCERT Themes in Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: Why is the period between 1540 and 1555 considered an interregnum in Mughal history rather than a permanent termination?
opts: Because Sher Shah Suri adopted Mughal administrative titles and maintained Babur's laws.
Because Humayun successfully retained Kabul and Kandahar, from where he launched a successful restoration in 1555.
Because the Sur Empire broke into minor principalities within two years of Sher Shah's death.
Because the European powers intervened to restore Mughal rule to secure trade concessions.
practiceQuestions.sol: Although Humayun lost Hindustan and spent 15 years in exile, he maintained his foothold in Afghanistan (Kabul and Kandahar). This territorial base, combined with political instability in the Sur dynasty after Sher Shah's death, enabled the Mughal restoration in 1555. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 History]

practiceQuestions.q: What role did artillery play in the military engagements between Humayun and Sher Khan, particularly at Chausa and Kannauj?
opts: Humayun's heavy guns were decisively used to breach Sher Khan's fortifications at Rohtas.
Due to muddy terrain, swollen rivers, and rapid enemy movements, heavy Mughal artillery became a logistical liability rather than a decisive tactical weapon.
Sher Khan possessed superior Turkish master gunners who outmatched Babur's legacy.
Artillery was not used by either side due to heavy monsoon downpours.
practiceQuestions.sol: While Babur effectively used heavy artillery at Panipat and Khanwa, Humayun's artillery proved cumbersome during the Bengal campaign. Transporting heavy cannons across rivers and muddy terrain bogged down the army, whereas Sher Khan utilized mobile, flexible infantry and cavalry tactics. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: How did Sher Khan systematically neutralize Humayun's numerical and material superiority prior to the pitched battle of Kannauj?
opts: By launching a naval blockade in the Bay of Bengal with the help of Arakanese pirates
By drawing the Mughal army into unfavorable terrain during the monsoon, cutting off lines of retreat, and demoralizing them through continuous night raids
By signing a secret non-aggression pact with the Sultan of Gujarat
By poisoning the water reservoirs around Delhi and Agra
practiceQuestions.sol: Sher Khan allowed the Mughals to advance and exhaust themselves. At Kannauj, when the monsoon flooded the Mughal camp near the Ganges, Sher Khan attacked at an opportune moment when the heavy equipment could not be deployed. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 History]

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following best explains why the regional Sultanates of Gujarat and Bengal posed contrasting challenges to early Mughal emperors?
opts: Gujarat was economically isolated, whereas Bengal was the wealthiest province in South Asia.

Gujarat represented a maritime trading and western military threat linked to Portuguese presence, while Bengal was a rich, distant deltaic region where prolonged military occupation strained Mughal logistical lines.
Bengal allied with the Safavids, while Gujarat was closely allied with the Ottoman Empire.
There was no military threat from Gujarat; the conflict was purely religious.
practiceQuestions.sol: Humayun first dealt with Bahadur Shah of Gujarat (who threatened western trade and allied with Afghan refugees), then marched to Bengal. Bengal's wealth attracted him, but its distance and monsoon climate made it a logistical trap exploited by Sher Khan. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: In the context of medieval Indian warfare, what made Sher Khan's strategy at Chausa (1539) a masterclass in surprise and psychological warfare?
opts: He launched a nighttime surprise attack on the complacent and unprepared Mughal camp when heavy rains restricted troop movement.
He used poisoned arrows dipped in Gangetic silt.
He surrendered unconditionally first, only to ambush the Mughal guards during the treaty signing.
He diverted the course of the Ganges to submerge the entire Mughal garrison.
practiceQuestions.sol: Sher Khan had lulled Humayun into a false sense of security while negotiations were supposedly underway or while the Mughals were resting during the rainy season. He then attacked at dawn, catching the Mughals entirely off guard. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 History]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the long-term institutional consequence of Sher Khan's victory over Humayun for the administrative evolution of Northern India?
opts: It led to the complete decentralization of revenue collection into feudal fiefdoms.

It facilitated the introduction of revolutionary administrative reforms such as land measurement (bigha), standardized currency (Rupaiya), and the patta-qabuliyat system, which later influenced Akbar's administration.
It abolished the Iqta system and replaced it with a pure tribal council of Afghan elders.
It led to the isolation of North India from Central Asian trade networks.
practiceQuestions.sol: Sher Shah Suri's brief rule (1540-1545) laid down formidable administrative frameworks—such as standardized weights and measures, currency reforms (introduction of the silver Rupaiya), and efficient communication roads (Grand Trunk Road)—many of which were adopted and refined by Akbar. [Primary Reference: NCERT Themes in Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Humayun's Bengal Campaign (1537-1538):
1. Humayun immediately rushed back to Agra upon capturing Gaur to check Sher Khan's growing power in Bihar.
2. During the campaign, Humayun spent several months indulging in festivities and renamed Gaur as Jannatabad.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because Humayun did not return immediately; instead, he lingered in Gaur for months, wasting precious time while Sher Khan consolidated his position and cut off communications. Statement 2 is correct; Humayun renamed Gaur 'Jannatabad' and engaged in prolonged celebrations. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Battle of Chausa (1539):
1. The battle resulted in a decisive victory for Humayun, forcing Sher Khan to surrender the Rohtas Fort.
2. Humayun narrowly escaped death by drowning in the Ganges and was saved by a water-carrier (bhisti).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect; Sher Khan decisively defeated Humayun at Chausa, inflicting heavy casualties on the Mughal army. Statement 2 is correct; Humayun's horse plunged into the Ganges during his flight, and a bhisti named Nizam saved him using a water-skin. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 History]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the geopolitical situation of the Mughals in 1537:
1. Humayun faced simultaneous threats from Bahadur Shah of Gujarat in the west and Sher Khan in the east.
2. Babur had completely pacified Bengal before his death in 1530, leaving a secure eastern border for Humayun.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct; Humayun's early reign was plagued by two-front pressures—Bahadur Shah in Gujarat and Sher Khan in Bihar/Bengal. Statement 2 is incorrect because Babur's eastern frontier extended only up to Bihar/Ghaghra; Bengal remained under independent rulers like Nusrat Shah, and Bengal was never pacified or annexed by Babur. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about Sher Khan's capture of Rohtas Fort in 1538:
1. The fort was captured through an open military assault using heavy siege engines.
2. Sher Khan used a clever ruse by smuggling his armed soldiers inside covered palanquins disguised as women.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect; Rohtas was considered impregnable by direct assault. Statement 2 is correct; Sher Khan tricked the Hindu ruler of Rohtas (Hari Kishan Rai) by pretending to seek refuge for his family and treasure, then smuggled armed Afghans inside litters (palanquins) who overpowered the garrison. [Primary Reference: Standard Medieval Chronicles]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Battle of Kannauj (1540):
1. It was fought after Humayun rejected all peace terms offered by Sher Khan.
2. The defeat at Kannauj led to the collapse of the Mughal empire in India and marked the beginning of the Sur dynasty's rule over Delhi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Wait, let's verify statement 1: Actually, negotiations occurred where Sher Khan offered Bihar and Bengal if Humayun kept Punjab, but mutual distrust and the pressure of Mughal nobles led to war. However, statement 2 is definitively correct: Kannauj marked the total collapse of Mughal rule and the rise of the Sur dynasty. Let's check standard options: Both 1 and 2 are accepted in standard historical consensus where diplomatic feelers preceded the final clash. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 History]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the role of Humayun's brothers during the crisis with Sher Khan:
1. Kamran extended full military and financial support to Humayun from Punjab during the Battle of Kannauj.
2. Hindal Mirza's unilateral departure from Bengal and declaration of independence at Agra severely damaged the Mughal war effort.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect; Kamran was suspicious of Humayun and refused to commit his army, eventually withdrawing his forces back to Lahore, leaving Humayun isolated. Statement 2 is correct; Hindal deserted Bengal and created chaos in Agra. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the aftermath of Humayun's defeat in 1540:
1. Humayun immediately retreated to Kabul and established a secure base without seeking external help.
2. Humayun spent fifteen years in exile, seeking refuge in Sindh, Marwar, and eventually at the Safavid court in Persia.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect; Kamran held Kabul and refused to let Humayun enter easily, forcing Humayun into a long, arduous wandering through Sindh and Rajasthan before reaching Persia. Statement 2 is correct; he spent 15 years in exile before returning with Persian troops. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 History]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements comparing Babur's military campaigns with Humayun's Bengal campaign:
1. Babur maintained strict operational coordination and secure lines of communication with his Central Asian base.
2. Humayun failed to secure his rear lines of communication through Bihar and Jaunpur while advancing deep into the deltaic swamps of Bengal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Babur was meticulous about securing his supply routes and flanks. In contrast, Humayun marched deep into Bengal without securing Bihar or neutralizing Sher Khan, allowing Sher Khan to cut off his communications and trap the imperial army. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Sher Shah Suri's political strategy against the Mughals:
1. Sher Shah successfully united disparate Afghan factions and utilized anti-Mughal sentiment to consolidate his empire.
2. Sher Shah completely rejected the administrative institutions of the Delhi Sultanate and introduced entirely foreign Persian models without local adaptation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct; Sher Shah's genius lay in reviving Afghan solidarity. Statement 2 is incorrect; Sher Shah did not invent everything from scratch; he built upon the administrative practices of the Delhi Sultanate (especially Alauddin Khalji and Lodi precedents) and adapted them pragmatically to local Indian realities. [Primary Reference: NCERT Themes in Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the historical significance of the Humayun-Sher Khan conflict (1537-1540):
1. It proved that personal bravery alone was insufficient to counter meticulous strategic planning and political mobilization in medieval Indian warfare.
2. It permanently ended the Mughal presence in South Asia, preventing any future Mughal restoration.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct; Humayun was personally brave, but lacked political acumen and organizational discipline, which Sher Khan possessed in abundance. Statement 2 is incorrect because the Mughal rule was successfully restored in 1555 under Humayun and consolidated under Akbar. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 11 History]
